sections.h2: What should a seller know about Pierce County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Pierce County is a rural southeast Georgia county with Blackshear as its seat. The county government says it was established in 1857 from land that belonged to Appling and Ware counties, and it was named for President Franklin Pierce. The Alabaha River winds through it, and its website points visitors toward fishing and the history of the Okefenokee.

It is the most spread-out county in the four-county Census comparison. QuickFacts lists 20,764 residents for July 2025, up 5.3 percent from the 2020 estimates base, across 340.46 square miles of land. That works out to 57.9 people per square mile in 2020. Only 68 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction is thin compared with the other three counties.

Prices reflect that. The median owner-occupied home was worth $153,300 for 2020 to 2024, 76.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the median gross rent was $799. Median household income was $60,517, and 82.9 percent of households have broadband. With values this modest, a delinquent tax bill can take a large share of a sale price, so a seller should find out the balance early.

sections.h2: Which Pierce County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Pierce County splits the work between the Tax Commissioner and the Board of Assessors, and both sit in county buildings on Nichols Street in Blackshear. The commissioner's own page says the office is independent of both the Board of Assessors and the Board of Commissioners, which keeps only budget control. The commissioner's main duty is to collect the taxes the assessors set.

The commissioner takes property tax payments online, and the site says online payments post on the next business day. Cards other than American Express are accepted with a convenience fee. A Georgia driver's license with a Pierce County address is required to title or tag a vehicle in the county.

sections.h2: What did the 2025 Pierce County millage notice say?
sections.html:
The county's millage page carries a notice that the Board of Commissioners tentatively adopted a 2025 rate requiring a property tax increase of 19.98 percent for unincorporated areas and 20.20 percent for incorporated areas. The hearings were held at the NFC Building at 705 College Avenue in Blackshear on November 6 and November 13, 2025, and those dates have passed.

Because the final rate can differ from a tentative one, ask the commissioner which millage appears on your bill, and ask whether your parcel sits in Blackshear, Patterson or an unincorporated area.

sections.h2: When is Pierce County property tax due?
sections.html:
Ask the Pierce County Tax Commissioner for the due date printed on your bill. The Georgia Department of Revenue explains the range: the official default is December 20, but a local government may adopt a resolution moving it to December 1 or November 15, or may bill in installments.

State rules give you some breathing room, and a few other facts help sellers:

  • Every taxpayer gets 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest begins to accrue, and later delinquent taxes may add penalties.
  • Pierce County property is taxed to the owner as of January 1.
  • Property tax returns are filed with the county tax office between January 1 and April 1.
  • Mobile homes in the county on January 1 must be returned by April 1, together with the location permit.

The commissioner's site also lists a tax sale registration form and an excess funds list. If your parcel is behind on payments, call 912.449.2026 before you list so you know how much to pay off at closing.

sections.h2: How does a Pierce County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
After the assessors set a new value, a notice goes to the taxpayer, who has 45 days to appeal in writing. The assessor's FAQ says late appeals are invalid. An appeal may rest on taxability, uniformity or value.

The appeal runs in stages:

  • The Board of Assessors reviews the appeal first and decides whether a change is warranted.
  • If nothing changes, the appeal goes to the Board of Equalization, an independent three-person board appointed by the Pierce County Grand Jury.
  • Either side may take the decision to Pierce County Superior Court.

Appraisers use cost, market and income approaches, and their field staff may visit a property to review an appeal, a return, new construction or a conservation application. They carry photo identification and drive a marked county vehicle. The Board of Assessors meets at least twice a month at 9:00 a.m., and the county asks you to schedule no later than the Friday before a meeting.

sections.h2: What exemptions and special assessments apply in Pierce County?
sections.html:
The Pierce County homestead exemption is available at the assessors' office year-round, but it must be filed by April 1 to reduce the current year's bill. You must own and live in the home on January 1, so a house bought after that date waits until the next year. Once granted, it stays in place until you move or the ownership changes. The Georgia Department of Revenue's county page says no local homestead exemptions are offered, so state exemptions are what applies; ask the assessors what your age or veteran status adds.

The assessor's FAQ lists special programs that can lower the value of land:

  • Preferential agricultural property is assessed at 30 percent of fair market value instead of 40 percent, with a 10-year commitment.
  • Conservation use assessment values bona fide farm and forest land at current use value.
  • Environmentally sensitive property and residential transitional property can also use current use value.
  • Standing timber is untaxed until it is sold or harvested, then taxed at 100 percent of fair market value.

Anyone selling acreage under a covenant should ask the assessors what a change of use or a sale does to the agreement before signing a contract.

faqs.q: Where is the Pierce County Tax Commissioner's office?
faqs.a: It is at 312 Nichols Street, Suite 4, in Blackshear, Georgia, with hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. Monday through Friday. The phone is 912.449.2026.

faqs.q: What is the Pierce County property tax due date?
faqs.a: Ask the commissioner or check your bill. Georgia's default is December 20, but a county may set December 1 or November 15, or use installments.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Pierce County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice, and the appeal must be in writing. The assessor's FAQ states that late appeals are invalid.

faqs.q: Can I pay Pierce County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. The commissioner accepts major cards except American Express, with a convenience fee, and online payments post on the next business day.

faqs.q: When must a Pierce County homestead exemption be filed?
faqs.a: By April 1 of the year you want the exemption. You must have owned and lived in the property on January 1 of that year.
